d050.t: A Guide to the Very End
msg: Today’s passage concerns the Graduate Guides, whom we will meet in Havona in the distant future. “⟦Q 24:6.3⟧The Graduate Guides are engaged in piloting the pilgrims of time through the seven circuits of Havona worlds.⟦/Q⟧” The passage promises that “⟦Q 24:6.3⟧the guide who greets you upon your arrival on the receiving world of the outer Havona circuit will remain with you throughout your entire career on the heavenly circuits.⟦/Q⟧”

What follows is even more moving. “⟦Q 24:6.3⟧Though you will associate with countless other personalities during your sojourn on a billion worlds, your Graduate Guide will follow you to the end of your Havona progression and will witness your entrance into the terminal slumber of time, the sleep of eternity transit to the Paradise goal.⟦/Q⟧” And upon awakening from that sleep, “⟦Q 24:6.3⟧you will be greeted by the Paradise Companion assigned to welcome you.⟦/Q⟧” Our journey, from beginning to end, is made in companionship.

This teaching shows an important truth that runs through the whole of The Urantia Book: we never ascend alone. On earth the Thought Adjuster indwells us, guardian seraphim watch over us, and the Spirit of Truth leads us. On the mansion worlds morontia companions are with us; in Havona, Graduate Guides and supernaphim; and on Paradise, a Paradise Companion (see Paper 25). At every stage of the ascent, loving companions are prepared for us.

Why has the universe provided companions with such care? Because the Universal Father loves us personally. We are not numbers processed in a vast administrative system, but personalities individually known and cared for. That one guide remains beside us throughout our whole Havona career shows how greatly the universe values the continuity of relationships. Love is not a passing kindness but a faithfulness that stays to the very end.

This truth is a comfort to our lives now as well. Sometimes we feel as though no one is beside us. But unseen companions are with us even now. Above all, the Thought Adjuster never leaves us for a single moment, whether or not we are aware of it. Just as a Graduate Guide will keep watch beside us in the universe future, so even at this moment the Father’s spirit is watching over us.

This teaching also shows us what kind of companion we should be to others. A Graduate Guide is not beside the pilgrim only when he succeeds, but accompanies him through the whole journey. We too can be such companions to our family, friends, and fellow believers. To stay near not only in good times but in hard times as well, to watch over and encourage a person’s growth to the very end: this is the way to become like the guides of heaven.

Today, let us remember with gratitude the unseen companions who share our life’s journey. And let us think of one person beside us who is walking a hard road. Let us ask ourselves whether we are being a companion who stays with him to the end, and today, even in some small way, let us remain at his side. Growing to resemble their faithfulness will be the most beautiful greeting we can offer the companions we shall one day meet in heaven. When we share with our neighbors the companionship we ourselves have received, the journey of ascent has already begun here on earth.
d050.pr: Today, contact one person who is walking a hard road and let him know that you are there for him.

msg: Today’s passage explains, from the standpoint of the universe, why misunderstanding and conflict arise in our world. “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧The moment the Creators bring into existence evolving individuals with the power of choice, that moment a departure is made from the smooth working of divine perfection; misunderstandings are certain to arise, and provision for the fair adjustment of these honest differences of viewpoint must be made.⟦/Q⟧” That is why the evolutionary universes have Conciliators. “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧No conciliating commissions need function in the central universe,⟦/Q⟧” but in the local universes they are indispensable.

The passage asks us to remember that “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧the all-wise and all-powerful Creators could have made the local universes just as perfect as Havona.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧But the Creators did not choose in their all-wisdom to do this.⟦/Q⟧” They “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧have produced universes which abound in differences and teem with difficulties,⟦/Q⟧” and “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧they have likewise provided the mechanisms and the means for composing all these differences and for harmonizing all this seeming confusion.⟦/Q⟧” A universe of differences is not a failure but an intended design.

Why did they do so? Because of free will. When beings who can choose for themselves come together, it is only natural that they should think differently. If everyone thought and acted exactly alike, that would be not freedom but mechanical uniformity. Because the Universal Father did not make us puppets, differences arise among us, and sometimes conflicts too. That is the natural consequence that comes with the gift of freedom.

Let us note that the passage uses the expression “⟦Q 25:3.7⟧honest differences of viewpoint.⟦/Q⟧” Not all conflict springs from malice. Many quarrels arise from different perspectives, different experiences, different understandings. Just because someone thinks differently from me, I need not conclude that he is evil. He may be thinking honestly in his own way. Merely acknowledging this softens many conflicts.

How, then, should we handle differences? The universe chose not to eliminate differences but to adjust them fairly. The Conciliators do not hear only one side; they examine the facts, understand both parties, and seek a fair settlement (see Paper 25, section 3). We too can learn this attitude in the face of conflict: seeking to understand one another rather than to win, and searching together for a fair resolution rather than insisting on our own position.

This teaching also comforts us that we need not fear conflict too much. When disagreements arise in a family or community, we easily feel that something has gone wrong. But differences are found wherever free personalities live together. What matters is not the absence of differences but the ability to handle them with love and wisdom. When conflict is handled well, relationships actually grow deeper, and we come to know one another better.

Today, let us think of someone whose views differ from ours. Let us try to see that difference not as hostility but as an honest difference of viewpoint. And let us try to understand his thinking from his own standpoint. When we become little conciliators, this universe so rich in differences moves one step closer to harmonious beauty. As the Conciliators preserve the order of the universe, so those who honestly acknowledge differences and deal with them fairly preserve the peace of families and communities.
d051.pr: Today, honestly set out once, from his own point of view, the thinking of someone who disagrees with you.

msg: Today’s passage portrays the scene of our arrival on Paradise in the distant future. “⟦Q 25:8.5⟧If you, as an ascendant mortal, should reach Paradise in the company of the companion or close associate of your earthly career, or if your seraphic guardian of destiny should chance to arrive with you or were waiting for you, then no permanent companion would be assigned you. But if you arrive alone, a companion will certainly welcome you as you awaken on the Isle of Light from the terminal sleep of time.⟦/Q⟧”

The passage says that careful provision is made in other cases as well. “⟦Q 25:8.5⟧Even if it is known that you will be accompanied by someone of ascendant association, temporary companions will be designated to welcome you to the eternal shores and to escort you to the reservation made ready for the reception of you and your associates.⟦/Q⟧” And the passage concludes: “⟦Q 25:8.5⟧You may be certain of being warmly welcomed when you experience the resurrection into eternity on the everlasting shores of Paradise.⟦/Q⟧”

How beautiful this scene is! At the end of so long a journey of ascent, we are not cast alone into a strange, cold place. Someone is waiting for us, calls us by name, and leads us to the dwelling prepared for us. The universe does not process our arrival indifferently; it welcomes us warmly. This shows what kind of heart the Universal Father has. He is the father who, seeing the prodigal son from afar, runs out to embrace him.

The part of the passage that especially touches the heart is its mention of the companion of our earthly career. The Urantia Book teaches that relationships of love formed on earth do not end in death. A spouse, a friend, or a co-worker with whom we walked the path of faith may reach Paradise together with us. Earthly friendship and love are precious relationships that can continue into eternity. So we should cherish and nurture our relationships with those who are beside us now.

The mention of the guardian seraphim also offers deep comfort. The guardian angel who watched over us on this earth may be waiting for us on Paradise (see Paper 113). That angel, who kept watch beside us without our knowing and walked the path of ascent with us, will be beside us at the end as well. We thought we were walking alone, but from beginning to end we had a companion.

This teaching also shows us how we should welcome others today. As Paradise welcomes us warmly, so we too can warmly welcome the newcomer, the stranger, and the one who has returned. To extend a heartfelt welcome to a neighbor who has just moved in, to someone attending a gathering for the first time, or to a family member returning after a long absence is to practice on earth, ahead of time, the welcome of heaven.

Today, let us picture the welcome that awaits us on the eternal shores. That hope becomes strength to endure today’s difficulties. And, in the likeness of that welcome, let us warmly receive one person we meet today. Those who share on earth the welcome they will receive in heaven are already living and breathing the air of Paradise. The small greeting of welcome we offer today is a foretaste of the great welcome we shall one day receive on the eternal shores. Those who have learned to welcome with love are ready to be welcomed with love. So let us treat those we meet today as guests of heaven.
d052.pr: Today, find one person who is a stranger or newcomer, and offer a heartfelt welcome with warm words.

msg: Today’s passage is one of the most stirring in The Urantia Book. “⟦Q 26:5.3⟧Long before reaching Havona, these ascendant children of time have learned to feast upon uncertainty, to fatten upon disappointment, to enthuse over apparent defeat, to invigorate in the presence of difficulties, to exhibit indomitable courage in the face of immensity, and to exercise unconquerable faith when confronted with the challenge of the inexplicable.⟦/Q⟧” And “⟦Q 26:5.3⟧long since, the battle cry of these pilgrims became: ‘In liaison with God, nothing — absolutely nothing — is impossible.’⟦/Q⟧”

This passage shows what kind of beings ascending mortals are. They are not people who ran from trials, but people who turned trials into spiritual nourishment. Uncertainty usually makes us anxious, but the pilgrims made a feast of it. Disappointment usually weakens us, but they fed on it and grew strong. The same difficulty can become either a poison that destroys us or a nourishment that makes us grow, depending on how we receive it.

Paper 26 says that when pilgrims arrive in Havona, they bring with them only one perfection, the perfection of purpose (see 26:4.13). Their faith has been tested, and they are known to be unshaken by disappointment. That steadfast faith did not suddenly appear in Havona. It was forged right here on this earth, and through the many stages of the mansion worlds and the local universe, by passing through countless uncertainties and disappointments.

The Urantia Book teaches that the uncertainties of the evolutionary worlds are essential to the growth of faith (see Paper 3, section 5). If everything were certain, there would be no need for faith. To believe in what is unseen and to trust God before an unknown future: that is faith. The uncertainty we now experience is therefore a training ground that strengthens the muscles of faith. This training, which cannot be had in the perfect worlds of Havona, is a precious opportunity for us.

The battle cry of the pilgrims should become our own confession: in liaison with God, nothing is impossible. This does not mean we can obtain everything we want. It means that for those who seek to do God’s will, no obstacle can be a final defeat. Even what looks outwardly like defeat becomes, for one joined with God, a path to a greater victory. So it was with the cross of Jesus.

Of course, we may not yet have attained such faith. We grow anxious before uncertainty, lose heart before disappointment, and shrink back before difficulty. But the passage says the pilgrims learned this. They were not like this from the start; they learned it through long experience. We too can begin to learn today. We need only start by entrusting one small uncertainty to God and finding a lesson in one small disappointment.

Today, let us call to mind one uncertainty that makes us anxious. And let us turn it into a feast of faith. Within this uncertainty I can learn to trust God more deeply. And let us shout the pilgrims’ battle cry in our hearts: in liaison with God, nothing is impossible. This confession is a little song to carry us through today, and a pilgrim’s banner raised toward eternity.
d053.pr: Write down one thing that makes you anxious today, and confess that in liaison with God nothing is impossible.

d054.t: Mercy, Evidence of the Indwelling Spirit
msg: Today’s passage sets two great quests side by side. “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧The mortal creature must find God. The Creator Son never stops until he finds man — the lowest will creature.⟦/Q⟧” Where man’s ascent toward God and God’s descent toward man meet, there takes place “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧this unique blending of the human and the divine, the commingling of creature and Creator.⟦/Q⟧” The passage says that “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧the Creator Sons and their mortal children are preparing for some future and unknown universe service.⟦/Q⟧”

These words bring balance to the direction of our faith. Our seeking of God is not the whole of faith. Before that, God is seeking us. Michael came to Urantia and descended to the very lowest place, seeking us like a shepherd searching for a lost sheep. Our seeking is a response to his seeking. When we set out to find him, he is already coming toward us.

The latter part of the passage contains a very important correction. “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧Unthinking mortals have referred to the manifestation of divine mercy and tenderness, especially towards the weak and in behalf of the needy, as indicative of an anthropomorphic God.⟦/Q⟧” In other words, they took it as evidence that God is sentimental and weak, like a human being. The passage points out what a great error that is: “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧What a mistake! Rather should such manifestations of mercy and forbearance by human beings be taken as evidence that mortal man is indwelt by the spirit of the living God.⟦/Q⟧”

This is a remarkable reversal of perspective. When we show mercy to our neighbors, it is not evidence that God resembles man, but evidence that man is coming to resemble God. Mercy is not human weakness but an expression of divinity. When the Thought Adjuster who indwells us moves us to mercy, “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧the creature is, after all, divinity motivated.⟦/Q⟧” In every moment of kindness and forbearance, God is being revealed within us.

The world often regards mercy as weakness and forbearance as incompetence. It thinks the strong must be cold, and that to succeed one has no room to look after the weak. But The Urantia Book teaches the very opposite. The mightiest God is the most merciful. Tenderness toward the weak is the surest sign that divinity is alive within us. So there is no need to be ashamed of mercy. It is evidence that we are children of God.

The passage says that Creator and creature together “⟦Q 26:11.5⟧traverse the gamut of the experiential universe and so are educated and trained for their eternal mission.⟦/Q⟧” This means our life is not a solitary journey but a journey shared with Michael. As he shared our experience, so we share in his mission. Even a single small mercy we show finds its meaning within that eternal partnership.

Today, let us practice mercy toward the weak and the needy. And let us remember that this mercy comes from the spirit of God within us. Every time we show mercy, God reveals himself to the world through us. The place where we who seek God meet the God who seeks us is the very place where mercy flows. Wherever the hand of mercy reaches, heaven and earth meet, and creature and Creator work together. That is the most beautiful cosmic co-operation in which we can take part every day.
d054.pr: Today, show a small mercy to one person in need, and remember that it came from God within you.

msg: Today’s passage defines worship concisely and profoundly. “⟦Q 27:7.1⟧Worship is the highest privilege and the first duty of all created intelligences. Worship is the conscious and joyous act of recognizing and acknowledging the truth and fact of the intimate and personal relationships of the Creators with their creatures.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 27:7.1⟧The quality of worship is determined by the depth of creature perception,⟦/Q⟧” and as knowledge of the infinite character of the Gods grows, worship becomes ever more all-encompassing until it eventually attains “⟦Q 27:7.1⟧the highest experiential delight⟦/Q⟧” known to created beings.

Let us first consider that worship is both privilege and duty. We often think of worship only as a duty, or, on the contrary, as an option we take up only when we feel like it. But the passage says worship is both. It is the first duty we rightly owe, and at the same time the highest privilege granted to us. What greater privilege could there be than to commune personally with the Creator of the universe?

The passage defines worship as the act of acknowledging the truth of an intimate and personal relationship. Worship is not a ritual of paying formal respect to an exalted being far away. It is realizing, and rejoicing in, the fact that the Creator has entered into an intimate and personal relationship with me. The Universal Father knows me, loves me, and dwells within me as the Thought Adjuster. To recognize and acknowledge this fact is the heart of worship.

Worship is also a conscious and joyous act. Worship offered under compulsion, worship that springs from fear, is not true worship. True worship wells up from joy. The more we come to know who God is, the more we cannot help but adore him. Just as admiration rises spontaneously before a beautiful landscape, so worship flows forth of itself when we perceive the character of God. Worship is less the result of effort than the fruit of realization.

The passage says that the quality of worship is determined by the depth of perception. If we know God shallowly, our worship is shallow; if we know him deeply, our worship deepens. The way to deepen worship, then, is to know God more deeply. As we study truth, meditate on the life of Jesus, commune with the Thought Adjuster, and discover God in our neighbors, our worship grows ever wider and deeper. Reading The Urantia Book, too, is ultimately for the deepening of worship.

The Urantia Book teaches that worship is pure adoration that asks for nothing (see Paper 5, section 3). Prayer may ask for something, but worship is loving God for God’s own sake. And such worship transforms us. We come to resemble what we worship. The more we worship God, the more we become like God, and that likeness overflows into service to our neighbors. Worship and service are the two wings of the spiritual life.

Today, let us stop everything for a moment and take time for worship that asks for nothing. Let us reflect on who God is and rejoice that he has entered into an intimate relationship with us. That brief moment of worship will become a light that hallows our whole day. A day begun in worship turns our work, our encounters, and our rest into a day spent with the Father. And as such daily worship accumulates, we learn in advance the full worship we shall one day enjoy on Paradise.
d055.pr: Today, for five minutes, ask for nothing, and simply worship, reflecting only on who God is.

msg: Today’s passage shows how fully known we are before the universe. “⟦Q 28:5.22⟧The Mother Spirit of Salvington knows you fully, for the Holy Spirit on your world ‘searches all things,’ and whatsoever the divine Spirit knows of you is immediately available whenever the secoraphic discerners reflect with the Spirit concerning the Spirit’s knowledge of you.⟦/Q⟧” We are not beings with nowhere to hide; we are beings fully known in love.

The passage, however, adds one important exception: “⟦Q 28:5.22⟧the knowledge and plans of the Father fragments are not reflectible.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 28:5.22⟧The discerners can and do reflect the presence of the Adjusters (and the Censors pronounce them divine), but they cannot decipher the content of the mindedness of the Mystery Monitors.⟦/Q⟧” The deepest communion between us and the Thought Adjuster who indwells us is kept as a divine secret that no reflective apparatus in the universe can look into.

These two facts give us two different comforts. The first is the comfort of being fully known. When we feel that no one understands us, the Mother Spirit knows us fully. She knows the conflicts of our hearts, the pain we cannot put into words, and the hopes we keep hidden. And she does not use that knowledge to condemn us, but to care for us. To be fully known and yet fully loved: that is the grace we enjoy.

The second is the comfort that between us and the Father there is a holy intimacy no one can intrude upon. The Thought Adjuster is a fragment of the Universal Father and is working out the Father’s plan within us. That plan and that communion belong to the Father and to us alone. Even the high beings of the universe cannot read them. This shows how personal and precious is the relationship the Father forms with each of his children (see Paper 18, section 1).

This truth makes our inner life a serious matter. Our minds are not spaces carelessly abandoned, but a holy sanctuary searched by the Holy Spirit and indwelt by the Thought Adjuster. We must therefore deal honestly with our thoughts and motives. The heart laid bare before God matters more than the appearance shown to others. Those who are honest before God are free before men.

This teaching also changes our attitude toward the inner lives of others. We cannot know another person’s heart completely. A Thought Adjuster dwells in that person too, and between him and the Father there is a holy communion we cannot know. We must therefore not judge others rashly. It is not our prerogative to measure a person’s soul by outward appearances alone.

Today, let us meditate on the fact that we are fully known. If there is something we want to hide, let us lay it before the One who already knows it and loves us still. And let us take time for quiet communion with the Mystery Monitor within us. In that holy place of meeting, which no one in the universe can look into, we enjoy the deepest peace. There, where the fear of being known turns into the assurance of being loved, we can stop pretending and live simply as we are, as children of the Father.
d056.pr: Today, honestly lay before God one feeling you have wanted to hide, and quietly commune with the indwelling spirit.

msg: Today’s passage is a very practical teaching about time. “⟦Q 28:6.9⟧Time is the one universal endowment of all will creatures; it is the ‘one talent’ intrusted to all intelligent beings. You all have time in which to insure your survival; and time is fatally squandered only when it is buried in neglect, when you fail so to utilize it as to make certain the survival of your soul.⟦/Q⟧” The passage explains this in connection with the ministry of the seconaphim called the Import of Time.

The expression “talent” calls to mind the parable Jesus told. The master entrusted different numbers of talents to his servants, but the servant who received one talent buried it in the ground and was rebuked (see Paper 176). The passage tells us that time is that one talent. Gifts, wealth, and circumstances differ from person to person, but time is given in common to every will creature. And it is our responsibility not to bury that time in the ground but to put it to use.

The most comforting part of the passage is its statement that “⟦Q 28:6.9⟧failure to improve one’s time to the fullest extent possible does not impose fatal penalties; it merely retards the pilgrim of time in his journey of ascent.⟦/Q⟧” God does not abandon us because we have failed to use every moment perfectly. We make mistakes, we idle, and we lose our way. But all of those losses can be recovered. The passage says plainly, “⟦Q 28:6.9⟧If survival is gained, all other losses can be retrieved.⟦/Q⟧”

What, then, matters most? It is making certain the survival of the soul. The most fatal way to squander our time is to let it slip away without seeking God and without choosing eternal life. Everything else is relative. The Urantia Book teaches that securing survival is not complicated. To desire sincerely to do God’s will and to have faith that trusts the Father: that is the way of survival (see Paper 5).

This teaching rescues us from two extremes. One is the laziness that lets time drift by unheeded. Life is not long, and postponing the decision for survival is dangerous. The other is the compulsion to use every moment perfectly. Such compulsion wears us out and makes us anxious. The passage teaches the balance between them: to be clear about what matters most, and to entrust the rest to God’s grace and to the time of eternity.

In the mansion worlds and in the ascending career beyond, we will have the opportunity to learn again much of what we missed on earth (see Paper 47). So there is no need to despair because we have not accomplished everything in our earthly life. But this does not mean we may treat our present time lightly. What we learn and choose here and now becomes the foundation of our eternal career. One hour well spent today reduces tomorrow’s delay and makes the eternal journey more joyful.

Today, let us remember that our time is a talent received from God. How much of our time today goes to things connected with eternity? Let us increase a little the time we give to prayer, love, learning, and service. And rather than reproaching ourselves for time wasted in the past, let us renew today the decision of faith that makes survival certain. Upon that decision, all other losses can be retrieved.
d057.pr: Set apart one hour of your day for something connected with eternity, such as prayer or loving service.

msg: Today’s passage speaks of beings we can hardly imagine. “⟦Q 29:0.11⟧Having knowledge about material creatures, you have at least a contrastive conception of spiritual beings; but it is very difficult for the mortal mind to envisage the power directors.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 29:0.11⟧In the scheme of ascendant progression to higher levels of existence you have nothing directly to do with either the supreme directors or the power centers. On certain rare occasions you will have dealings with the physical controllers, and you will work freely with the supervisors of morontia power upon reaching the mansion worlds.⟦/Q⟧”

The whole of Paper 29 shows that the physical energies of the universe never move blindly. The power directors, power centers, and physical controllers transform, manipulate, and direct the energies of the universe (see 29:3.6). The courses of the stars and the flows of energy are not products of chance; they are under the intricate supervision of living, intelligent beings. Behind the regularity of the universe that we call natural law are the unseen hands of order.

This fact gives us deep grounds for trust. We take it for granted that the sun rises every morning, that the seasons turn, and that physical laws operate consistently. Yet that dependability rests upon the faithful service of countless beings. The universe is not chaos but order, and that order comes ultimately from the Universal Father on Paradise. The reliability of the physical world reflects the faithfulness of the One who governs it.

The passage also teaches humility. Beings we cannot even picture are at work in the universe. Our knowledge, compared with the vastness of the universe, is only a tiny fragment. Science has revealed much, yet there remain in the universe realities beyond our imagining. A mind that can be humble before what it does not know is a mind ready to receive greater truth.

The last part of the passage lets us glimpse our future. Upon reaching the mansion worlds, we “⟦Q 29:0.11⟧will work freely with the supervisors of morontia power.⟦/Q⟧” Beings who are hard to imagine now will then become our colleagues. The ascending career is a journey of continually meeting new beings, learning new realities, and moving into wider dimensions of the universe. Our understanding does not end here and now; it will go on widening throughout eternity.

This teaching also speaks to our everyday lives now. In our lives, too, there are many hands keeping order where we cannot see them. Like the people who supply electricity, purify water, and clean the streets, they serve without our noticing, and we live by their service. When we think of the unseen service of the power directors, we also grow grateful to the unseen servants around us.

Today, let us look afresh at one order we have taken for granted. As we see the air we breathe, the rising sun, and the flowing water, let us think of the faithful hands behind them. And let us give thanks to the Universal Father, the source of all that order. Those who trust the unseen hands that keep order can enjoy deep peace even in a confused world. Trust in the order of the universe leads at last to faith in the goodness of the Father who established that order.
d058.pr: Today, call to mind one order of nature you have taken for granted, or one person who works unseen, and express your gratitude.

msg: Today’s passage tells us the important fact that intelligence and personality are not the same. “⟦Q 29:4.13⟧Personality is not necessarily a concomitant of mind. Mind can think even when deprived of all power of choice, as in numerous of the lower types of animals and in certain of these subordinate physical controllers.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 29:4.13⟧Many of these more automatic regulators of physical power are not persons in any sense of the term.⟦/Q⟧” They are not endowed with will and independence of decision, yet “⟦Q 29:4.13⟧all of them are highly intelligent beings.⟦/Q⟧”

This short paragraph speaks with special meaning to us today. We tend to think that the capacity to think and calculate is the core of being human. But the passage says that intelligence alone does not make a personality. There are beings who are highly intelligent yet have no freedom of choice. They carry out their assigned tasks perfectly, but they do not choose for themselves what to do. The core of personality is not the magnitude of intelligence but the capacity for free choice.

The Urantia Book teaches that personality is a gift bestowed directly by the Universal Father (see Paper 16, section 8). Personality is distinct from mind and higher than mind. Personality is the capacity to choose with a will, to be self-conscious, to enter into relationship with other personalities, and to know and love God. And it is because of this very personality that we can survive and walk the eternal ascending career. However brilliant our intelligence may be, without personality the road to eternity would not open.

This truth changes the way we see ourselves. We often measure a person’s worth by intelligence, education, or ability. But by the standard of the universe, human dignity lies in the personality received from the Father. Those who are not intellectually gifted, those who are sick, little children: all alike are honorable beings endowed with personality. Before God, a person’s worth is revealed not by the size of the intellect but by the sincerity of his choices toward God.

This teaching also awakens us to how we should live. We have the capacity to choose, yet we can leave it unused and live like machines. To live reacting automatically, according to habit, impulse, and the expectations of others, is to live as though we had no personality even though we possess one. A truly personal life is a life of choosing with an awakened will. When we choose for ourselves what to do, how to respond, and whom to serve, we realize the dignity of personality.

The passage says that these beings are “⟦Q 29:4.13⟧wholly subservient to the mechanical perfection of design for the tasks of their allotment.⟦/Q⟧” Their perfection is beautiful, but it is not the result of choice. Our perfection, by contrast, has not yet been attained, but it is something we achieve by choosing. When an imperfect but free being chooses God’s will for himself, he adds to the universe a value more precious than mechanical perfection.

Today, let us look at the areas in which we live by automatic reaction. And in those areas, let us make awakened choices. To pause and choose when anger rises rather than reacting out of habit, to decide by will rather than following impulse in the face of temptation: this is the way to live as a being endowed with personality. Each of our choices becomes a grateful response to the gift of personality the Father has given us.
d059.pr: Today, at one moment when you would usually react out of habit, pause and choose differently with an awakened will.

msg: Today’s passage explains what happens to us after death: the mystery of resurrection. “⟦Q 30:4.15⟧The physical body of mortal flesh is not a part of the reassembly of the sleeping survivor; the physical body has returned to dust. The seraphim of assignment sponsors the new body, the morontia form, as the new life vehicle for the immortal soul and for the indwelling of the returned Adjuster. The Adjuster is the custodian of the spirit transcript of the mind of the sleeping survivor. The assigned seraphim is the keeper of the surviving identity — the immortal soul — as far as it has evolved.⟦/Q⟧”

The passage says that resurrection takes place when these two reunite the personality trusts committed to them. “⟦Q 30:4.15⟧When these two, the Adjuster and the seraphim, reunite their personality trusts, the new individual constitutes the resurrection of the old personality, the survival of the evolving morontia identity of the soul.⟦/Q⟧” And so “⟦Q 30:4.15⟧such a reassociation of soul and Adjuster is quite properly called a resurrection, a reassembly of personality factors.⟦/Q⟧” We do not vanish in death. Our true self is safely entrusted to the hands of two faithful custodians, and it awakens again on the mansion worlds.

This teaching deeply comforts our fear of death. Many people fear death as the end of everything. But The Urantia Book teaches that death is not an end but a transition. The body returns to dust, but the spiritual values we have gathered on this earth and the soul that has evolved are preserved. The Thought Adjuster keeps the spiritual content of our minds, and the guardian seraphim keeps our soul (see Paper 112). Even while we sleep, we are never abandoned and alone.

The passage also gives us a right understanding of the body. The physical body is not part of the resurrection. The weakness of the body, its illnesses, disabilities, and aging, therefore do not determine our eternal identity. This body is a precious instrument for life on earth, but it is not our true self. Even as the body grows frail, the soul can grow, and even when the body returns to dust, the soul goes on growing in a new morontia form. This is a great hope for those who are sick and growing old.

Yet the passage honestly confesses that “⟦Q 30:4.15⟧even this does not entirely explain the reappearance of the surviving personality.⟦/Q⟧” In resurrection there remains a mystery we cannot understand. And the passage concludes: “⟦Q 30:4.15⟧Though you will probably never understand the fact of such an inexplicable transaction, you will sometime experientially know the truth of it if you do not reject the plan of mortal survival.⟦/Q⟧” Resurrection is not something to be proved by theory, but a truth to be known by experience.

There is one important condition here: “⟦Q 30:4.15⟧if you do not reject the plan of mortal survival.⟦/Q⟧” God does not force survival upon us. Survival depends on our choice. But that choice is not difficult. It is to desire sincerely to do God’s will, to trust the Father, and to live a life that chooses spiritual values. For those who live such a life, resurrection is not a fearful unknown but a joyful promise.

Today, let us quietly meditate on death and resurrection. If we carry the pain of having let a loved one go before us, let us remember that he is safely entrusted to the hands of faithful custodians. And thinking that we too shall one day awaken on the mansion worlds, let us gather spiritual values today in preparation for that day. The love and truth we choose today will awaken with us on the morning of resurrection.
d060.pr: Today, decide on one spiritual value you want to take with you when you awaken on the mansion worlds, and put it into practice.

d061.t: Many Mansions in the Father’s House
msg: Today’s passage reveals the meaning of a famous saying Jesus left us. “⟦Q 30:4.17⟧Sometimes all training worlds of mortal residence are called universe ‘mansions,’ and it was to such spheres that Jesus alluded when he said: ‘In my Father’s house are many mansions.’⟦/Q⟧” And the passage explains that “⟦Q 30:4.17⟧within a given group of spheres like the mansion worlds, ascenders will progress individually from one sphere to another and from one phase of life to another, but they will always advance from one stage of universe study to another in class formation.⟦/Q⟧”

These words of Jesus have long been cherished as words of comfort. Many have understood them as a vague promise that there is a spacious house in heaven. But The Urantia Book tells us that the words point to a far more concrete reality. After death we awaken on actual training spheres called the mansion worlds, and there we learn and grow in what we did not fully learn on earth (see Paper 47). The Father’s house is not a static resting place but a living school.

The method of this school is very interesting. Within a group of spheres, each advances individually at his own pace. Some learn quickly, some slowly. God does not require the same pace of everyone. Each person’s individuality and needs are respected. Those who learned late on earth, and those who come bearing many wounds, can grow step by step on the mansion worlds at a pace suited to them.

But when passing from one great stage of universe study to the next, ascenders always advance together “⟦Q 30:4.17⟧in class formation.⟦/Q⟧” This shows that the ascending career is not a solitary journey but a shared one. We grow as individuals, but we advance as a community. Those who learn quickly help those who learn slowly, and when all are ready together, together they move on to the next stage. The universe beautifully harmonizes individuality and community.

This principle applies just as much to our religious life now. Growth in faith is each person’s own task. No one can pray for me or know God for me. Yet faith does not grow in isolation. In a community that learns together, prays together, and encourages one another, we go farther. A heart that wants to go far together is closer to the spirit of the ascending career than a heart that wants to go fast alone.

This teaching also renews the meaning of the companions with whom we now study and share our faith. Those who read and meditate on The Urantia Book with us today may perhaps be our classmates on the mansion worlds and in the many stages beyond. Spiritual friendships formed on earth may be the beginning of an eternal class. So let us cherish those who walk with us and rejoice in their growth as if it were our own.

Today, let us take to heart the promise that there are many mansions in the Father’s house. Our journey does not end on this earth; it continues on through many schools. So let us not be impatient, but learn what there is to learn today. And let us reach out a hand to the companions who walk with us, helping one another so that we can advance together to the next stage. The Father’s house is wide and the road within it is long, but because we walk together, we do not grow weary.
d061.pr: Today, offer a word of encouragement to a companion on the path of faith, and pray for his or her growth.

msg: Today’s passage explains what the mortal finaliters are. “⟦Q 31:3.6⟧The mortal finaliters have fully complied with the injunction of the ages, ‘Be you perfect’; they have ascended the universal path of mortal attainment; they have found God, and they have been duly inducted into the Corps of the Finality.⟦/Q⟧” But the passage immediately points to three things they have not yet attained. “⟦Q 31:3.6⟧Such beings have attained the present limit of spirit progression but not finality of ultimate spirit status. They have achieved the present limit of creature perfection but not finality of creature service. They have experienced the fullness of Deity worship but not finality of experiential Deity attainment.⟦/Q⟧”

This passage reveals an astonishing truth: even beings who have reached Paradise and found God still have room to grow. To have reached perfection does not mean to have reached the end. It means having reached the limit of the present stage, and beyond it new horizons still lie open. Life in the universe never stagnates. When we climb one summit, a higher summit comes into view.

The injunction the passage cites, “⟦Q 1:0.3⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect,⟦/Q⟧” is the starting point of our ascending career (see Paper 1). At first hearing, this command seems impossible. How can we, so weak and so full of mistakes, become perfect? Yet the mortal finaliters prove that the command can actually be fulfilled. Beings of animal origin, passing along the long road of ascent, at last fully complied with it. That road is open to us as well.

At the same time, the passage teaches that perfection comes in stages. Even at this moment we can pursue the perfection suited to each stage. What is required of us in earthly life is not the perfection of Paradise but perfection of purpose, a sincere desire to do God’s will (see Paper 26, section 4). If that purpose is sincere, we are already standing on the path of perfection. Perfection is not reached all at once; it is achieved anew at every stage.

This teaching guards us against spiritual pride. Just because we have gained some insight or reached some stage of faith, we must not think we have achieved it all. If even the finaliters of Paradise have not yet attained finality, how much more must we still learn! The humble are always learning, and those who learn are always growing.

At the same time, this teaching gives us boundless hope. The journey before us has no end. It is not a tedious eternity, but an eternity filled with ever-new service, ever-new learning, and ever-new worship. The Corps of the Finality is even now waiting and preparing for service in the universe ages to come. Our destiny is not to stop at perfection but to go beyond perfection into greater service.

Today, let us consider what perfection we can attain at our present stage. Not a grand goal, but one sincere purpose to do God’s will today. Those small perfections will accumulate, until one day we too, as members of the Corps of the Finality, shall know the joy of having found God. And even then, still higher horizons will be calling us.
d062.pr: Today, choose one small perfection you can attain right where you are, and carry it out with a sincere heart.

msg: Today’s passage gathers the whole journey of evolutionary mortals into a single sentence. Evolutionary mortals are born on the planets of space, pass through the morontia worlds, ascend the spirit universes, traverse the Havona spheres, find God, attain Paradise, and are mustered into the primary Corps of the Finality, there to await the next assignment of universe service. And Grandfanda, the first mortal ascender, presides as chief of all orders of finaliters. Before this sublime spectacle the author of the paper exclaims: What a glorious destiny for the animal-origin children of time, the material sons of space!

This exclamation is the wonder of a high being of the universe as he looks upon us. He does not hide our point of departure. We are children of animal origin, beings born on a material world. Yet it is precisely because of that lowly beginning that our destiny is all the more glorious. A journey that begins in the lowest place and arrives at the highest: that is the ascending career of a mortal. Our glory lies not in having been high from the start, but in rising with God from the depths.

The story of Grandfanda testifies that this destiny has actually come true. He was the first mortal pilgrim to find Havona (see Paper 24, section 6), and now he stands at the head of all finaliters. One mortal walked that path first, and countless mortals have followed after him. We too are invited to join that procession. Before us lies a road already walked by multitudes of pilgrims who went ahead.

Each stage of this journey connects with the picture of the universe we have explored from Paper 16 through Paper 31. The Seven Master Spirits and the family of the Infinite Spirit who care for us, the Ancients of Days who govern us, the Sons of God who have come down for our sake, the angels and messengers who guide us: all these beings work for a single purpose. That purpose is to help the mortal of animal origin find God and reach Paradise. The whole universe is cooperating in our ascent.

And yet the passage tells us that arrival at Paradise is not the end. There the finaliters await their next assignment of universe service. The Urantia Book intimates that finaliters will one day serve in the new universes now being organized in outer space (see 31:10.16). Our eternal destiny is not to rest in repose, but to serve, sharing with ever-wider universes the love we have received. For the one who has received to become the one who gives: that is the fulfillment of a glorious destiny.

This magnificent destiny is not unrelated to our small day today. The road to Paradise begins here and now, on this planet. The prayer I offer today, the kindness I show today, the truth I choose today: these are the first steps of that eternal journey. Being born on a planet of space is only our starting point, not a limit that confines us. The Thought Adjuster within is leading us toward that destiny.

Today, let us make the passage’s exclamation the confession of our own hearts: What a glorious destiny! When we are worn and weary, when we feel insignificant, let us remember these words. A destiny that moves even the high beings of the universe to wonder is waiting for us. With gratitude for that destiny, let us live this day as one more step toward Paradise.
d063.pr: Whenever you feel weary or small today, confess silently in your heart, “⟦Q 31:10.20⟧What a glorious destiny!⟦/Q⟧”

msg: Today’s passage shows us in a word what kind of being God is: God is not a self-centered personality. Though the Universal Father possesses infinite power, he does not clutch it to himself; he freely distributes himself to his Sons and to his creatures. Whatever another being is able to do, he entrusts to them, and he waits patiently while they grow in the doing of it. This is God’s way, and it holds just as true of the Creator Son who rules a local universe as of us mortal men living on a small world.

As Paper 32 explains how a local universe evolves over long ages, it reveals the attitude of the Father behind the whole process. The Father entrusts the universe to Michael, the Creator Son, and Michael in turn distributes the work among multitudes of Sons and spirits. This chain of delegation is not a parceling out of power but an extension of love. To entrust is to trust, and to trust is to believe that the other can grow. That is why the passage calls this bestowal the outworking of the ideal and infinite love of the Universal Father. God works in this way because he wants his creatures to be not merely recipients of benefits but co-workers with him. One who is given nothing to do cannot grow; only one who bears responsibility gains experience. God’s delegation is therefore both the highest respect he could show us and an invitation to grow.

The passage goes one step further. If God has withheld aught of himself from the universal creation, then even of that residue he is bestowing upon us the Thought Adjusters. The Thought Adjuster is a pure fragment of the Universal Father who so patiently indwells the mortal mind and leads us toward God (see Paper 107). There can be no clearer proof of the Father’s magnanimity than this: that the Infinite One personally dwells within the mind of the smallest creature.

This truth teaches us two things for our lives. First, we are never forsaken. The Father is not a distant ruler but one who has placed himself within us, so that in every circumstance we are accompanied by a divine inner companion. Second, to become like God is to become one who shares as God shares. Not to clutch our time, our talents, and our understanding, but to entrust them and to wait patiently while others grow: that is how divine love is practiced on earth.

Another section of this paper explains that while the Father does not directly intervene in the affairs of a local universe, he is never withdrawn from it. Through the personality circuit he is directly connected with every personality, and through the Adjuster he is personally present within our minds. To entrust is not indifference but deep respect. As a parent gives a child the chance to try things alone while always watching from close by, so the Universal Father gives us the opportunity to grow through experience and is with us through every step of the process.

Today, look at what you are holding onto alone. To entrust to another, at home or at work, what they are able to do, and to share gladly what you have received, may seem small things, but they reflect the character of the Universal Father. As those who have received the love of a Father who gives himself without reserve, may we too become channels through which that love flows on.
d064.pr: Today, gladly share with someone else one task or talent you have been keeping to yourself.

msg: The closing section of Paper 32 declares that there is a great and glorious purpose in the march of the universes through space. Today’s passage proclaims that this purpose is for each one of us. There is in the mind of God a plan which embraces every creature of all his vast domains, and this plan is an eternal purpose of boundless opportunity, unlimited progress, and endless life. And the passage insists that its treasures are ours for the striving.

The words that follow ring out like a starting signal: The goal of eternity is ahead! The adventure of divinity attainment lies before you! The race for perfection is on! There is no qualifying examination for this race. Whosoever will may enter. Origin, station, and past failures do not matter. All that is needed is the will to enter, the sincere choice to do the will of God. Our part is to renew each day the choice to enter the race. God has already opened the way, and the door stands open to everyone. More often than not, what holds us back from the race is not some outward obstacle but our own hesitant hearts.

This is not a race we run alone. The passage tells us that we run depending every step of the way on the leading of the indwelling Adjuster and on the guidance of that good spirit of the Universe Son, the Spirit of Truth, which so freely has been poured out upon all flesh. The Thought Adjuster points within us to the will of God, and the Spirit of Truth awakens our minds to truth. Because these two divine helpers are with us, certain victory is promised to every human being who will run the race of faith and trust.

Here we learn the perspective of eternity. Earlier sections of this paper say that the segments of time are like flashes of personality, and that eternity cannot be fully fathomed by the finite mind. Today’s difficulties or slow growth are only one stretch of an eternal race. A single fall does not decide the whole race. What matters is direction, the daily decision to get up again and walk toward God. God’s plan already embraces us, so our part is to cooperate willingly with that plan.

Hearing this promise, we may be tempted to regard it as a story about some distant future. But the passage says the race is already on. Our eternal career does not begin after death; it began the very day we chose to seek God. Life on this earth is the first stretch of that long journey, and the decisions we make here carry over into the mansion worlds and the career beyond (see Paper 47). That is why no single day is ever trivial. Boundless opportunity and unlimited progress unfold from right here and now, and in every moment we are taking part in that eternal purpose.

So welcome this day as a day of eternal adventure. A small kindness, an honest choice, a single quiet prayer: each is a step in the race for perfection. When you grow weary or discouraged, remember the promise that the race is already on, that One walks with you from within, and that the crown of victory is certain. The treasures of eternal life lie open to those who strive.
d065.pr: If you stumbled today, see it as one stretch of the eternal race and decide on the next step with which to begin again.

msg: Paper 33, explaining how a local universe is administered, introduces Michael, the Creator Son, who stands at its center. Today’s passage says that the Creator Son is the vicegerent personalization of the Universal Father, the divinity co-ordinate of the Eternal Son, and the creative associate of the Infinite Spirit. And it declares that to our universe and all its inhabited worlds the Sovereign Son is, to all practical intents and purposes, God. This means that the way for us to know and meet God is never far away.

Finite mortals cannot fully comprehend the infinite Deities of Paradise as they are in themselves. So the Universal Father has placed a Creator Son in each local universe to personify all of the Paradise Deities which evolving mortals can discerningly comprehend. Michael is the face of God to us. As Jesus of Nazareth he came to our world in human flesh, and through his life he showed us what the Father is like (see Paper 120). He who has seen him has seen the Father. Many of our misunderstandings about God arise from thinking of him as too distant and abstract. But the Universal Father sent the Creator Son precisely to bridge that distance. Because of him, we can now love the infinite God without fear.

The passage also says that this Son and his Spirit associate are our creator parents. Michael cares for our existence as a father, and the Universe Mother Spirit, the Divine Minister, as a mother. We are not orphans in the universe. We have parents who made us, who know us, and who desire our growth. This truth turns our faith from an abstract doctrine into a living relationship.

If we apply this truth to life, we need not think of drawing near to God as something difficult. Instead of wearing ourselves out trying to fathom the infinite God, we can look at the life of Jesus and strive to love as he loved. When we meditate on how he treated the sick, the mercy with which he received sinners, and his wholehearted devotion to the Father’s will, we come to know God most closely. And all the while the spirit of the Divine Minister who cares for us holds our hearts steady.

Paper 33 also explains that Michael’s sovereignty was not complete from the beginning but was earned experientially through seven bestowals. He lived in the likeness of several orders of creatures, and finally he was born and lived as a mortal man on Urantia. Our creator parent, then, does not know our life only from the outside. He personally went through hunger and weariness, misunderstanding and loneliness, and even death. When we pray, we are speaking to one who has already been through our circumstances, and who therefore understands us deeply. This makes our approach to God all the lighter and more confident.

Today, begin your day by thinking of Michael, the sovereign of our universe, as your creator parent. Rather than shrinking before the Father’s infinity, give thanks for the way that infinity has drawn near to us. And to take one trait of God’s character that you have come to know through Jesus and live it out today: that is how to live this passage.
d066.pr: Recall one scene from the life of Jesus that stays with you, and live it out once today.

msg: Today’s passage beautifully portrays the relationship between the two divine personalities who lead a local universe: the Creator Son and the Creative Mother Spirit. The Son functions as a father in his local universe, and the Spirit enacts the role of a mother, always assisting the Son. In the administration of the universe the Spirit is everlastingly indispensable. The two personalities take different roles, but they are partners bringing a single work of creation to fulfillment.

The passage explains how this partnership appears in the crisis of rebellion. To contest rebellion and retrieve what was lost is the task of the Son and his associated Sons. The Spirit does not confront rebellion directly, but she ever sustains the Son in all that he may be required to experience on worlds tainted with evil. And the passage concludes that no Son could hope for final success without the incessant co-operation of the Divine Minister and her vast assemblage of spirit helpers, the daughters of God. We draw comfort from this. Michael’s healing of the wounds of rebellion was never a lonely struggle, and neither is the restoration now going forward on our world. Countless beings of heaven and earth are working with one heart for the spiritual recovery of this world.

Our world, Urantia, is just such a world, touched by rebellion (see Paper 53). So this passage is not a description of universe administration unrelated to us. Michael lived his bestowal life on our world and overcame the consequences of rebellion, and throughout that whole process the spirit of the Divine Minister and innumerable angels helped him. Even today the seraphim and the spirit helpers so faithfully and valiantly struggle for the welfare of mortal men. We are living in the midst of an unseen cooperation of love.

In this passage we learn a spirituality of cooperation. Even the highest divine personalities do not work alone; they respect each other’s roles and work together. So it is in our families and communities. We need those who lead and those who help, those who stand in front and those who support from behind. Steady service in unnoticed places is never small. Just as the incessant co-operation of the daughters of God is essential to the success of the universe, our quiet devotion is a necessary part of God’s work.

Another thing worth noting in this passage is that different roles do not imply superiority or inferiority. That the Son takes on the task of confronting rebellion does not make the Spirit any less important. On the contrary, the passage stresses that without the Spirit’s co-operation no Son could hope for final success. Paper 34 explains that after Michael completes his seventh bestowal, the Creative Mother Spirit is recognized as co-ruler of the local universe. The order of the divine worlds is not competition but mutual complementarity, and the whole is completed when each functions fully in his or her own place. The relationships of our lives, too, grow healthy and beautiful as they come to resemble this divine pattern.

Today, think of the people you work alongside. If you are in a place of leadership, treasure the labors of those who help; if you are in a place of helping, remember that your service is a participation in God’s work. As the Son and the Spirit work as one, may we too become co-workers who build one another up.
d067.pr: Think of one person who helped you behind the scenes today and offer them a word of thanks.

msg: Today’s passage opens with one of the most beloved sayings in The Urantia Book: The Spirit never drives, only leads. God does not drag us along by force. When we are willing learners, when we want to attain spirit levels, when we sincerely desire to reach the eternal goal, then the divine Spirit will gently and lovingly lead us along the pathway of sonship and spiritual progress.

Why does the Spirit never drive? Because God has given us free will. Love that is forced is not love, and a choice made under compulsion is no true choice. The passage says that every step we take must be one of willingness, intelligent and cheerful co-operation. The domination of the Spirit is never tainted with coercion. This shows how deeply our personality is respected. God waits for us to come to him because we ourselves desire it. He does not want us to obey like robots; he wants us, as beloved children, to choose his will for ourselves. That is why the leading of the Spirit always waits for our consent. In that waiting lie God’s deep patience and respect.

Paper 34 deals with the Local Universe Mother Spirit and the ministry of that Spirit within us. Within us the spirit of the Divine Minister, the Spirit of Truth, and the Thought Adjuster are all at work. The second part of the passage says that when a life of spirit guidance is freely accepted, there gradually develops a positive consciousness of divine contact and assurance of spirit communion. And it gives a fresh interpretation to the scriptural words that the Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. Because the Adjuster has already told us of our kinship to God, the Spirit bears witness “⟦Q 34:6.12⟧with your spirit,⟦/Q⟧” not to your spirit.

These words bring great comfort to our life of faith. The assurance of being a child of God is not something someone else certifies for us or something we manufacture by force; it grows naturally within a life that responds freely to the leading of the Spirit. These words also teach us how to treat others. If even God does not compel, we cannot force our faith upon our families or neighbors. We can only show it through love and gently invite.

The Spirit’s leading usually does not come through dramatic experiences. It appears as a quiet assurance, an inner pull toward a better choice, a longing within to love and to forgive. Each time we obey these small promptings, our spiritual sensitivity grows a little, and our communion with the Spirit becomes clearer. Conversely, if we keep ignoring those promptings, our ears gradually grow dull. That the Spirit never drives also means that our choices carry all the more weight. So spiritual growth comes not through one great decision but through the steady habit of responding willingly to the small leadings given each day.

Today, listen for the voice of the Spirit gently leading within your heart. That voice never shouts or threatens. It simply shows, quietly, a better way. As you respond to its leading willingly and cheerfully, you will find the assurance of being a child of God growing deeper and deeper within.
d068.pr: Today, notice any moment when you are about to force your views on someone, and turn it instead into a gentle word of suggestion.

msg: Paper 34 closes with a majestic word of encouragement. Today’s passage is both a command and a promise to those of us who have started out on the way of life everlasting. We have accepted the assignment and received our orders to advance. Therefore, the passage says, do not fear the dangers of human forgetfulness and mortal inconstancy, do not be troubled with doubts of failure or by perplexing confusion, do not falter and question your status and standing. For in every dark hour, at every crossroad, the Spirit of Truth will always speak, saying, “⟦Q 34:7.8⟧This is the way.⟦/Q⟧”

Just before this passage, Paper 34 deals frankly with the conflict between the flesh and the spirit. We were born with a nature of animal origin, and our world has suffered the double disaster of rebellion and the Adamic default. Yet the passage says that in spite of all these difficulties, spirit-born men and women can live on a higher plane as faith sons. Our weakness does not define us. What defines us is our status as children of God, and that is not shaken by our feelings or our failures. Our standing does not rise and fall with our emotions. Our sonship with God was settled the moment we accepted it by faith, and the one who keeps it secure is not ourselves but God. With that assurance we can rise again without fear of failure.

Consider the three fears the passage names. The first is forgetfulness and inconstancy: we forget our resolutions, and our hearts change easily. The second is doubt of failure: the anxious question of whether we can really go all the way. The third is doubt about our status: the question of whether someone like me could truly be a child of God. To all these fears the passage gives a single answer: the Spirit of Truth is with us and will show us the way.

The Spirit of Truth, poured out upon all flesh after Jesus departed, brings his life and teachings vividly alive in our minds (see Paper 194). When we stand at a crossroad not knowing which way to take, we can ask what Jesus would have done, and the Spirit of Truth quietly answers that question. The dark hours may not disappear, but even in the darkness we are not alone. One who knows the way is walking with us.

The moments when we feel lost usually come when we try to see too much at once. The Spirit of Truth does not show us the map of our whole life at a glance. Instead it lights up the next step we need to take now. So the voice saying “⟦Q 34:7.8⟧This is the way⟦/Q⟧” is not every answer about the future but enough light for today. Faith is walking in trust of that light, and as we walk, the next step is lit in turn. As we go forward step by step in obedience, we look back and realize how faithfully God has led us. Doubt grows when we stop walking and shrinks when we move our feet.

If doubt or fear shakes your heart today, slowly turn these words over in your mind. We have already started on the way of life everlasting, and we have received our orders to advance. So do not hesitate; take the next step. With every step, the Spirit of Truth will whisper, “⟦Q 34:7.8⟧This is the way.⟦/Q⟧”
d069.pr: Today, whenever a decision lies before you, pause a moment and quietly ask what Jesus would have done.

msg: Paper 35 introduces the Sons of God born in the local universe, and it gives the first place to the Melchizedek Sons. Today’s passage says that the Melchizedeks are the first order of divine Sons to approach sufficiently near the lower creature life to be able to function directly in the ministry of mortal uplift, to serve the evolutionary races without the necessity of incarnation. They stand just about midway between the highest Divinity and the lowest creature life of will endowment. They thus become the natural intermediaries between the higher spiritual levels of existence and material life.

This middle position is deeply meaningful. A being too high can hardly feel the plight of those below, and a being too low can hardly convey lofty truth. Because the Melchizedeks stand where they can understand both, they honor the will of the Creator Son above and discern the needs of evolving creatures below. The passage says that all forms of intelligent life find in these Sons understanding friends, sympathetic teachers, and wise counselors. Even the seraphim delight to work with them. Paper 35 adds that the Melchizedeks are nearly perfect in wisdom but not infallible in judgment. Because they are beings who can make mistakes, they understand erring creatures all the better. It is not perfection but sympathy that makes them excellent teachers.

The Melchizedeks are in charge of the educational system of the local universe, and many of the schools through which ascending mortals pass, beginning on the mansion worlds, are under their direction (see Paper 45). In the life after death we will meet these wise teachers. And in the history of our own world, Machiventa Melchizedek appeared at Salem in the days of Abraham and kept alive the spark of faith in one God (see Paper 93). He was a friend who came directly to our human race.

This passage shows us what a good teacher and a good friend are. Such a one is not someone who teaches while looking down from above, but someone who comes down to where the other stands, understands, sympathizes, and walks alongside. Much knowledge alone does not make a good teacher; truth is conveyed only when one can enter into another’s situation. The Melchizedeks are revered not only for their wisdom but because they carry that wisdom in sympathy.

In daily life we too can become a bridge for someone. As those who have walked the path of faith a little longer, we can draw near to someone still searching for the way, speak in his language, understand his pain, and quietly show him higher values. To seek first to understand before trying to teach, and first to listen before giving advice: that is how we come to resemble the spirit of the Melchizedeks. Beside such a person, people feel not judged but understood, and in that understanding they finally open their hearts. Those who are understood find strength to stand on their own. When we listen to someone all the way through, the spirit already at work within that person can speak more clearly.

Today, think of one person around you who needs help. Rather than trying to hand them the right answer, become a friend who thinks things through with them from where they stand. Understanding friend, sympathetic teacher, wise counselor: these three faces of the Melchizedeks are what all of us can become for one another.
d070.pr: Today, when someone shares a burden with you, be a friend who listens all the way through before offering any advice.

msg: Today’s passage shows us another face of the Melchizedek Sons. They are the first to act in all emergencies of whatever nature on all worlds where will creatures dwell. Sometimes they serve as temporary custodians on wayward planets, acting as receivers of a defaulting planetary government. When need be they make themselves visible to mortals, and seven times in Nebadon a Melchizedek has served on an evolutionary world in the similitude of mortal flesh. The passage calls them the versatile and volunteer emergency ministers to all orders of universe intelligences and to all the worlds.

The word in this passage that stays with me most is volunteer. When a crisis strikes, the Melchizedeks do not go reluctantly because someone orders them; they step forward of their own accord and go where help is needed. Though they are a self-governing order, they use their freedom for service. They possess high wisdom and ability, yet they do not use them for their own glory; they gladly devote them to helping the worlds in the direst straits.

Our own world, Urantia, is a world that has received just such help. After the rebellion of the Planetary Prince, Caligastia, and the default of Adam and Eve, our world was plunged into spiritual darkness. At that time Melchizedek receivers took charge of planetary affairs, and at last Machiventa Melchizedek appeared in human form and taught the truth of one God at Salem (see Paper 93). The spark of truth he kindled was carried on through Abraham and later prepared the way for Michael to come to this world. Our spiritual heritage owes a great debt to that volunteer service.

This passage teaches us the attitude of service. Crises always come without warning, and in those moments people wait for someone to step forward. Many draw back, saying it is not their business, or wait for others to move first. But the way of the sons of God is to move first. To be like the Melchizedeks, drawing near first wherever need appears, humbling ourselves to fit the situation, and standing as custodians over what has broken down: this is the mark of a mature soul. Seen this way, the very history of our faith rests on the volunteer devotion of one Melchizedek. Had he not stepped forward in that moment of crisis, faith in one God might have flowered far later. The willing decision of one being changed thousands of years of history.

Of course, we cannot take charge of universe emergencies. But in the face of a family crisis, a friend’s trouble, or a community’s hardship, we can become small emergency ministers. Visiting someone who is sick, calling someone who is discouraged, calmly bringing order in the midst of confusion: all of these count. What matters is not the size of our ability but a heart willing to step forward. When that heart is present, God accomplishes great things even through our small hands. A little courage shown in a moment of crisis often becomes a grace remembered for a lifetime. The hand we hold out may feel to someone like the very hand of God.

Today, look around you to see whether someone is waiting for help. And instead of waiting for others to step forward, take the first step toward them yourself. The first to come in a crisis: that is the picture of a son of God that the Melchizedeks show us in the universe.
d071.pr: If you learn today of someone in difficulty, do not wait for someone else to step forward; reach out to them first.

msg: Paper 36 is devoted to the Life Carriers, and today’s passage makes a clear declaration at its very opening: life does not originate spontaneously. Life is constructed according to plans formulated by the Architects of Being and appears on the inhabited planets as a result of the operations of the Life Carriers of the local universes. The Life Carriers are intrusted with designing and carrying creature life to the planetary spheres, and after planting this life on such new worlds, they remain there for long periods to foster its development.

This declaration offers an important balance to modern thinking. We often try to understand life merely as the product of chemical reactions that happened by chance. The Urantia Book does not deny that life evolves. On the contrary, it explains in detail how life developed from simple to complex forms over hundreds of millions of years (see Paper 65). But it says that intelligent planning and care stood at the beginning of that evolution and guided its direction. Evolution is God’s method, not a substitute for God.

The last sentence the passage speaks about the Life Carriers is especially moving. They do not plant life and then leave. They remain on that world for long ages, watching life grow and fostering its development until will creatures appear. On our world too, after the Life Carriers planted life some 550 million years ago, they tended this earth through long ages until the appearance of man. The very fact that we exist is the fruit of that long patience and care. The Life Carriers not only plant life but consider in advance in what environment it will flourish best. They study the physical conditions of the planet, select the life patterns suited to that world, and prepare the way for that life one day to blossom into beings endowed with moral will. The whole history of life is, in effect, one long story of care.

When we take this truth to heart, the way we look at life changes. A blade of grass by the roadside, a bird outside the window, and above all the person beside us: each is a life that was planned and cared for. If life were a product of chance, perhaps we could treat it carelessly; but if life is a gift of intelligent love, we must revere it and hold it dear. Reverence for life touches upon reverence for God.

This passage also awakens us to the worth of our own existence. When life feels meaningless, or when you feel like a being tossed into the world by accident, remember these words: life does not originate spontaneously. Our physical life came from the long labors of the Life Carriers, our personality from the direct gift of the Universal Father, and the Adjuster within us from the very spirit of God. In no respect are we the result of chance. A heart that respects life leads in the end to worship of the One who gave life. In the hands that cherish even one small life, we gradually learn the heart of the Creator.

Today, look upon the living things around you with new eyes. Breathing, the beating of your heart, waking in the morning: think of all these as the fruit of long planning and care, and give thanks. Those who have received life as a gift must become those who care for life.
d072.pr: Today, as you walk or look out the window, gaze for a long moment at one living thing and give thanks for life.

msg: Today’s passage deals with a somewhat unfamiliar concept, the adjutant mind-spirits. The adjutant mind-spirits are seven mind influences that the Local Universe Mother Spirit bestows upon the living creatures of the evolutionary worlds: the spirits of intuition, understanding, courage, knowledge, counsel, worship, and wisdom (see Paper 36, section 5). The passage says that while these adjutants are in no manner directly related to the spirit of the personal presence of the Divine Minister, the Holy Spirit of the inhabited worlds, they are functionally antecedent to, and preparatory for, the appearance of this very spirit in evolutionary man.

Here lies a deep insight into God’s way of creating. God does not make finished spiritual beings from the start; he prepares them step by step, from lower levels to higher. In animals the first five adjutants operate, giving the capacities of intuition, understanding, courage, knowledge, and counsel. In man the spirits of worship and wisdom are added. When these seven spirits have functioned sufficiently that man becomes capable of moral judgment, then the Holy Spirit comes and the way opens for the Thought Adjuster to indwell.

The passage adds that the adjutants do not repercuss in the Supreme Being when acting on prepersonality levels. This means that the activity of a merely animal mind does not yet leave eternal value behind. But when a human being uses that mind to seek God and choose the good, that choice takes on spiritual value and leaves an eternal mark in the universe. Our minds began in animal origins, yet they were designed to be open toward spirit. In this way God’s creation does not skip stages. Just as a seed puts forth a sprout and raises a stem before it blooms, so the mind first lays its foundation and only then becomes ready to receive the higher ministry of spirit. In this orderly sequence lie the Creator’s wisdom and patience.

This teaching greatly helps us understand ourselves. Within us dwell both an instinctive mind bent on survival and a spiritual longing for God. At times we suffer from the tension between the two. But the passage tells us that even this lower mind is part of the process that prepares for the higher spirit. Our intellect, emotions, and courage are not things to be cast away but gifts of God to be rightly used under the leading of the spirit.

The spirits of worship and wisdom, in particular, are the decisive gifts that distinguish human beings from animals. The spirit of worship causes us to look up to a being greater than ourselves, and the spirit of wisdom moves us toward orderly and progressive development. When we feel awe and seek the right way, these adjutants are at work within us. When we cherish and cultivate those small stirrings, the higher ministry of the Holy Spirit and the Adjuster comes to flower within us. So the work of governing our thoughts and feelings is not separate from the spiritual life. The effort to cultivate the mind rightly is the very work of lovingly preparing a home where the spirit may dwell.

Today, treasure the awe and the longing for wisdom that rise in your heart. The moment you marvel at something beautiful or feel the desire to do what is right, that is a moment when the spirit is preparing the way within you. God uses the whole of our minds to lead us to himself.
d073.pr: Today, notice the moments when awe or wonder rises in your heart, and pause briefly to give thanks.
